solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Touched soft material

blocks.note: first meaning: past tense of feel, to handle or sense by contact
second meaning: a fabric made of matted, pressed wool fibres

explanation.surface: Someone running a hand over a piece of soft cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the past tense of feel, meaning handled, and the name of a matted woollen fabric.

clue.text: Copy one that can't fly behind

blocks.note: the emu is a large flightless Australian bird
behind schedule means late

explanation.surface: An instruction to imitate a flightless creature trailing at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: To emulate someone is to imitate or match them, so it is a verb synonym of copy.

clue.text: Old volunteer army producing letter from Greece

blocks.note: the article always said with this force's name, which 'old' marks as no longer current
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's part-time volunteer reserve, renamed the Army Reserve in 2014

explanation.surface: A former reserve force somehow generating a letter sent from Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole phrase 'Old volunteer army' really means the TA, as the force was called before 2014; it is split here only to show the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth character of the Greek alphabet, written as a circle with a bar.

clue.text: Man in chinos tearing round US city

indicators.note: something tearing is ripped apart, so the letters of the trousers are rearranged
going round something means surrounding it, so the rearranged letters enclose the city

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: A man in casual trousers rushing around an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicholas is a man's first name, so 'man' stands for it as an example of a male name.

clue.text: Coming up, forbid arrest

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: to ban is to forbid

explanation.surface: A warning that a ban on arrests is on its way.
explanation.definitionFit: To nab someone is informal for catching or arresting them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Having mixed fortunes, sort of flag

blocks.note: first meaning: a career with ups and downs is described this way
second meaning: the black-and-white squared flag waved at the end of a motor race

explanation.surface: A racing driver's career of ups and downs, finished under that flag.
explanation.definitionFit: A history marked by alternating success and failure is called this, and so is the squared flag used in motor racing.

clue.text: A month back, new plane shape

blocks.note: OCT is the calendar abbreviation for October
back, as in two years back, means ago
N is the standard abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A month ago a new aircraft had some shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plane' suggests an aircraft, but here it is the geometry sense: a flat figure.
explanation.definitionFit: An octagon is an eight-sided polygon, a figure drawn in a flat two-dimensional plane.

clue.text: Keenly expectant, with nothing in abundance

blocks.note: agog means eagerly waiting
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone eagerly waiting while having plenty of nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A gogo, from French, means galore or in plentiful quantity, an adverbial phrase like 'in abundance'.

clue.text: Dominant woman, perhaps Victoria B

blocks.note: Victoria is an example of a queen, signalled by 'perhaps'
the letter B is spelt out as it is said

explanation.surface: Victoria Beckham, perhaps, as a dominant woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Victoria B suggests Victoria Beckham, but it is read as Queen Victoria followed by the letter B written out in full.
explanation.definitionFit: A queen bee is idiomatic for a woman who dominates or leads her social circle.

clue.text: Use horn, coming and going

blocks.note: a word that is the same whether it comes forward or goes back, read left to right or right to left

explanation.surface: A driver sounding the horn while arriving and leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: To toot is to sound a horn briefly, so it is a verb meaning to use one.

clue.text: Opening of hostilities, also known as the rugby challenge

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: the first letter of hostilities
aka is the standard abbreviation for also known as

explanation.surface: The start of a war, also called the rugby challenge.
explanation.definitionFit: The haka is the Maori war dance performed by the New Zealand rugby team before a match as a challenge.

clue.text: The way to encourage a caviare producer

blocks.note: ST is short for street, a way
to urge on is to encourage

explanation.surface: Advice on how to encourage a fish farmer making caviare.
explanation.definitionFit: Caviare is the salted roe of the sturgeon, so this fish produces it.

clue.text: Plan to bring huge pastries over

indicators.note: turned over means flipped end to end, so in this down clue the words are read from the bottom up

blocks.note: mega means huge
tarts are pastries

explanation.surface: A scheme for delivering enormous cakes.
explanation.definitionFit: A stratagem is a cunning scheme or ploy, so a plan in a crafty sense.

clue.text: Hot stuff very quietly eaten by earl?

indicators.note: what is eaten goes inside the eater, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: an earl is an example of a peer, hence the question mark
pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quiet

explanation.surface: A nobleman swallowing something spicy without fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepper is a hot spice, so it is fairly described as hot stuff.

clue.text: Sort of hat one could eat? Or just swallow?

blocks.note: first meaning: a flat-topped hat with a turned-up brim
a savoury pastry filled with meat, a further meaning tucked in between
rhyming slang for a lie, something a gullible person might swallow or believe

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a hat might be eaten or simply gulped down.
explanation.walkthrough: Three meanings: the hat, the meat pastry, and Cockney rhyming slang pork pie for lie, which one 'swallows' by believing it.
explanation.definitionFit: A pork pie is a style of hat, and in rhyming slang a lie, a falsehood someone might believe.

clue.text: Not stay for the decisive contest

blocks.note: first meaning: to flee or depart rather than remain
second meaning: a deciding race or vote after a tie

explanation.surface: Leaving early instead of staying for the final.
explanation.definitionFit: To run off is to leave hurriedly, and a run-off is a further election or race that settles a tie.

clue.text: So far we failed, as predicted

indicators.note: something that failed has broken down, so these letters fall into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A rueful admission that our efforts have so far failed, just as expected.
explanation.definitionFit: To have foreseen something is to have anticipated it, a past-tense synonym of predicted.

clue.text: Motorway got on the nerves, so went elsewhere

blocks.note: the M1, Britain's main north-south motorway, written with I for 1
something that grated irritated

explanation.surface: Someone driven away by an irritating motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds or people that migrated moved to another region, so they went elsewhere.

clue.text: I must meet old, pale statesman

blocks.note: taken as written
O is a standard abbreviation for old
wan means pale

explanation.surface: Someone due to meet an elderly, pallid politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Statesman' looks like a politician, but it means a man from a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: An Iowan is a native of Iowa, a state of the USA, so a 'state's man' in a punning sense.

clue.text: Mad for a bushy hairstyle

indicators.note: mad suggests crazed disorder, so the following letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone keen on a big, bushy hairstyle.
explanation.definitionFit: An Afro is a rounded, thick hairstyle of tightly curled hair, which is bushy.

clue.text: Legal to be beheaded? That's terrible

indicators.note: beheading removes the head, so the first letter is cut off

blocks.note: lawful means legal

explanation.surface: Outrage that beheading might be within the law.
explanation.definitionFit: Awful and terrible are adjective synonyms for very bad.

clue.text: Exchange hands when returning

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the word is read right to left

blocks.note: paws is informal for hands

explanation.surface: Players changing hands as they come back.
explanation.definitionFit: To swap is to trade one thing for another, a verb synonym of exchange.

clue.text: Inhabitant of bowl, proverbially very public

definitions.text: Inhabitant of bowl, proverbially very public

blocks.note: the surface reading: a creature that lives in a round glass tank
the setter's reading: living in this creature's bowl is the idiom for a life with no privacy

explanation.walkthrough: The saying 'living in a goldfish bowl' describes a life lived in full public view.
explanation.definitionFit: The pet fish kept in a glass bowl gives its name to the idiom for complete lack of privacy.

clue.text: Undisciplined, goes without speaking

indicators.note: speaking means the phrase is heard rather than read, so the sound counts

blocks.note: someone who goes without something lacks it

explanation.surface: A sloppy person who keeps quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Lax means slack or careless about rules, an adjective synonym for undisciplined.

clue.text: During school time, nine of the Romans mingle

blocks.note: in means during, as in in the night
a school term is a period of teaching
IX is nine in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Pupils in Latin class mixing during the term.
explanation.definitionFit: To intermix is to blend together, a verb synonym of mingle.

clue.text: Fine fabric that may be watered?

blocks.note: first meaning: a very fine linen or cotton cloth
second meaning: an area of mown grass, watered with a sprinkler

explanation.walkthrough: Watered silk is a known fabric finish, so 'watered' seems to continue the textile; it is the garden grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawn is a sheer linen cloth and also the grassed area of a garden, which gets watered.
